name: Little Red-Cap
description: A little girl loved by everyone receives a cap of red velvet from her grandmother. Her mother sends her through the wood with cake and wine for the sick old woman and orders her not to leave the path. The Wolf distracts her with flowers, reaches the house first, devours the Grandmother, and lies in her bed wearing her clothes; he then swallows Red-Cap as well. A Huntsman hears the snoring, cuts open the beast's belly with scissors, and rescues them both. Red-Cap fills the Wolf with stones, and he falls dead when he wakes. Later, the girl and her Grandmother defeat a second wolf together without straying from the road again.

info.name: Little Red-Cap
info.ability: Once per day, choose a player and learn whether they register as a character other than their real character.
info.lore: A little girl loved by everyone who sees her, and most of all by her grandmother, who gives her a cap of red velvet. She carries cake and wine through the wood, leaves the path to gather flowers, and is swallowed by the Wolf; rescued from his belly, she carries the stones that bring him down and learns never again to disregard her mother's warning.

presentation.title: Little Red-Cap
presentation.description: Choose a player and privately compare their real character with the character they register as.

info.name: Mother
info.ability: Each night, after the Wolf, choose a player. At dawn, learn whether they were Devoured or digested when the Wolf took a disguise that night.
info.lore: A prudent woman who prepares cake and wine for her sick mother. She tells Red-Cap to walk carefully, stay upon the path, greet her grandmother upon entering, and not peer into every corner first; her voice opens the tale and turns each woodland detour into a warning remembered too late.

cues.body: After the Wolf, the Mother chooses a player. At dawn, show Yes if they were Devoured or digested for a disguise tonight; otherwise show No.
After the Wolf, the Mother chooses a player. At dawn, show Yes if they were Devoured or digested for a disguise tonight; otherwise show No.

presentation.title: Did the Wolf reach them tonight?

info.name: Grandmother of Little Red-Cap
info.ability: On your first night, learn which player is Little Red-Cap.
info.lore: A sick old woman who lives alone half an hour into the wood, beneath three great oaks and near the hazel-trees. The Wolf lifts the latch, swallows her, and puts on her clothes; the Huntsman draws her out alive though scarcely able to breathe. During the second encounter she understands the trick, has the door barred, and makes Red-Cap fill a stone trough with sausage-water until another wolf falls in and drowns.

cues.body: Point out to the Grandmother the player who is Little Red-Cap.

info.name: Huntsman of Little Red-Cap
info.ability: Each night, before the Wolf, choose a player without learning whether they are Devoured. If they are, free them and restore their ability.
info.lore: A huntsman passing the cottage who recognizes something strange in the supposed Grandmother's snores. He finds the old enemy he has long sought, but lowers his gun in case the woman still lives; with scissors he opens the sleeping belly, draws out Red-Cap and then the Grandmother, and goes home carrying the Wolf's skin.

cues.body: Before the Wolf, the Huntsman chooses a player. If they are Devoured, remove that state and wake them to announce the rescue.

info.name: Flower Seller
info.ability: Once per game, before the Wolf, you may prepare a lure. If the Wolf chooses to Devour that night, you are Devoured instead of the chosen target. If the Wolf takes a Disguise, the lure is spent without effect.
info.lore: A figure imagined from the flowers that lead Red-Cap away from the path while sunlight crosses the trees and birds sing. She knows which posies catch the eye and which scents can turn a beast aside; when she prepares her lure, the tale's distraction becomes a deliberate sacrifice for one night.

cues.body: Before the Wolf, ask whether the Flower Seller prepares her lure. If she does, mark the use and redirect any Devoured state caused by the Wolf tonight to her.
If her ability remains, before the Wolf ask whether the Flower Seller prepares her lure. If she does, mark the use and redirect any Devoured state caused by the Wolf tonight to her.

prepareFlowerLure.question: Does the Flower Seller prepare her lure tonight?

info.name: Miller
info.ability: Once per game, when an execution is about to resolve, you may change its target to another living player.
info.lore: A figure imagined from the hamlet where the previous day was baking-day and the cake beneath Red-Cap's apron was made. Used to sending flour down forking roads and turning a wheel with diverted water, he can change at the last moment the person toward whom his neighbors' judgment leans.

presentation.label: The Miller redirects the execution
presentation.title: Miller
presentation.description: Choose another living player to receive the execution that was about to resolve.

info.name: Forest Lad
info.ability: Once per day, publicly mark a player. If they become Devoured that night, at dawn learn a {{team:grimm:oscuro}}.
info.lore: A youth imagined as the Huntsman's apprentice, long engaged in tracking the old Wolf. He reads bent grass, trampled flowers, and mud beside the hazel-trees; when he announces publicly where he thinks the beast will pass, he risks his name to preserve a trail that may lead to the creature's true lair.

cues.body: If there is a public Wolf's Trail, after the Wolf check whether that player was Devoured tonight. If so, at dawn point out a {{team:grimm:oscuro}} to the Forest Lad.

info.name: Wolf
info.ability: Each night, choose a player and either Devour them or take a Disguise. A Devoured player remains alive but has no ability; if someone was already Devoured, that player dies. To take a Disguise, the Devoured player dies, you learn their real character, and you register as them. If you die, any Devoured player is freed.
info.lore: A cunning beast who greets Red-Cap courteously, asks where she is going, and judges that the child will be a finer mouthful than the old woman. He turns her aside with flowers, runs straight to the cottage, imitates her voice, swallows the Grandmother, and lies in her bed wearing cap and clothes. His hunger ends beneath the weight of stones, though the tale remembers that another wolf comes after him.

cues.body: The Wolf chooses Devour or Disguise and points to a player. Devour disables the new target's ability and digests the former occupant; Disguise requires the Devoured player, kills them, and manually fixes their real character as the Wolf's registered identity.

wolfNightChoice.question: What does the Wolf do tonight?

options.label: Devour

info.name: Fox
info.ability: On your first night, learn a {{team:grimm:oscuro}}. You do not die or lose your ability when a {{team:grimm:oscuro}} dies.
info.lore: An accomplice imagined from the cunning the tale gives to woodland beasts. He does not belong to the Wolf's pack, but recognizes his trail, bargains with his hunger, and carries rumors from den to den; his loyalty is born of opportunity, and so he survives when the predator he aided falls beneath the stones.

cues.body: Point out a {{team:grimm:oscuro}} to the Fox.

info.name: Hound
info.ability: When the Wolf takes a Disguise, learn which player was digested to provide it. Your ability continues to work if the Wolf dies.
info.lore: A hound imagined beside the Huntsman who has long sought the Wolf. He can distinguish the scent of a borrowed cap, hide beneath a gown, and a trail that ends too suddenly at a bed; even if the predator dies, he keeps the identity of the prey whose scent the Wolf tried to wear.

cues.body: After the Wolf, if he took a Disguise tonight, point out to the Hound the player who was digested to create it.
After the Wolf, if he took a Disguise tonight, point out to the Hound the player who was digested to create it.

info.name: Stones in the Belly
info.ability: The first time a Devoured player would die from an ability, they leave the belly alive instead of dying.
info.howToRun: Keep the Blessing visible. The first time an ability would kill a Devoured player, cancel that death. Resolve their release and the removal of the Devoured state normally. The Blessing is then spent.

category.description: Optional rules that gently tilt the tale toward Evil.

info.name: Off the Path
info.ability: At the start of the first night, a player secretly chosen by the Storyteller begins Devoured; the Wolf knows who they are.
info.howToRun: Before characters act, secretly choose a living player and make them Devoured. Their ability is restricted like any other occupant of the belly. Wake the Wolf and show them who begins inside their belly.

nightInstructions.opening: Make sure every player has closed their eyes. Resolve the Flower Seller's lure and the Huntsman's rescue before the Wolf; resolve the Mother, Hound, and Forest Lad only after the Wolf has chosen.
nightInstructions.dawn: Release expired woodland marks, wake the village, announce deaths, and privately deliver every report that was waiting for daylight.
